utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do have a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me clarify a few points of your background. First of all, the two documents you were shown which relate to -- to 1992, one was authored by Ibrahim Hukic and the other one by General Enver Hadzihasanovic. At that time, you didn't see those documents. It's the first time, I take it, when you were proofed by Mr. Ibrisimovic, that's the first time you saw those documents, but not in 1992 or 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Let me tell you, it was really a long time ago. I can't be 100 per cent certain whether I saw these documents for the first time during proofing or I saw them maybe at the time when they were written. From this distance in time, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you said that you were part of the TO -- no, of the 333rd mountain Brigade and then at one time, I think it was in March of 1993, you got transferred to the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade. Now, can you be a little more specific? At what time did you actually become member of the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: That was certainly in the last few days of March. I cannot tell you the exact date but I know it was the end of March.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you also told us that at one time, the headquarters of the battalion moved from that school to the Motel Sretno, can you tell us approximately, if you recall after such a long time, when the headquarters was moved?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see again, it was a long time ago and I can only say that I suppose it was in April. I cannot claim anything with any certainty because it was really a long time ago. I would be happy to tell you the truth if I was certain, but all I can tell you it was maybe in April, the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many people were working or were part of the headquarters, were working on those offices that were first located in the school and then in the motel?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you see, it was called a battalion but in reality, I don't think the battalion had even 30 per cent of the prescribed personnel, according to establishment. When I joined it, it was in the process of slow establishment. There were a lot of posts still vacant as far as commanding officers were concerned and as for the troops, we had two companies or so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: In those headquarters, was there a commander, a deputy commander, a chief of staff, who was there?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: When I joined the battalion, the commander was Catic. I forgot his first name, maybe somebody can remind me. His last name was Catic, I forget his first name now. So he was battalion commander when I joined. The Chief of Staff was not at all envisaged, according to establishment. There was a deputy commander, Kasim Alajbegovic, and I really don't know about the Chief of Staff. I don't think there was supposed to be one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the commander's first name, Nihad Catic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Nihad, you are correct. Nihad Catic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: He was removed, wasn't he, sometime in June, towards the end of June; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end of June, I remember there was some transfers within the unit, personnel changes within the brigade, and I believe this Catic left for Zenica on another brigade post, I don't know which, but he was not replaced. That much I know. At that point, even I was transferred to a different battalion but I don't think anybody was replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So you don't know that your commander, Mr. Catic, was removed for failing to carry out an order to prevent crime and looting in the Kakanj area? That's not something you had heard at that time?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: You must believe me if I say that I really don't know anything about it. Nobody informed me personally whether it was a simple staffing change or it was some sort of punishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Of the members of the battalion staff, was there a person called Saban Zunic who was a operations officer?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know these men for sure. The name does not ring a bell. I'm not aware of anybody in Kakanj named Zulic in our battalion, 99 per cent of men came from the municipality of Kakanj, from the town of Kakanj. Zunic or Zulic, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Saban H. Zunic, you've never heard of him.

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me go on to that afternoon in May 1993, and I don't think you told us a date. Perhaps you can't but can you place it ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think to this last question, the witness answered that he is not aware of this first and last name but I don't think his answer was recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kulovic, can you please tell us whether you are aware of a person called Saban H. Zunic who was part of the -- any military formation in Kakanj in May 1993?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let me turn to those events about military police who came from Zenica and the beatings. Can you tell us a little bit more what time it was, what date it was, to start with, because you were quite precise about what time of day it was in the afternoon. Do you know more about the date? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I think -- I don't know. Was it 18th May, some other date? You see, I can't be certain which date it was. I believe it was in the second half of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... perfectly okay, your answer. Now, you said these military police from the brigade came from Zenica. Do you remember who was the chief of the police who came with them to Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I did not see the chief of police. Those policemen came alone. I didn't even see them when they arrived. I was inside when they arrived and they dropped by to take something and I heard from two of them where they were going. I didn't know either of the men personally, I just saw military police insignia on their arms. They had those white belts, the regular military police equipment and uniform, but I didn't know any of them personally, I didn't see their chief and I'm not aware whether he accompanied the group or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And how many were there? How many members of the military police who showed up at your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I didn't see them all, but from what I heard and found out, it is 10 to 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you told us that there were some troops around the hotel in and around the motel, and can you tell us what troops were there?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I am not quite clear about this question, what troops -- what troops do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes. You told us that the military police came and they then went to that plant and then some members of the military police came back, and then you said that the troops around the motel started to panic. And I'm merely asking you to at the us what troops these are, what formations, to whom do they belong?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Those troops were not around, they were within the facility, troops from the 3rd Battalion of the 7th Muslim Brigade. And since our municipality is Kakanj, our own soldiers were afraid for their families in case a conflict broke out, they were afraid that there might be fighting between the Croatian villages and us, and I have to tell you that since -- from when we were established, there were many, many provocations by the HVO in the Kakanj area. This was just one in a long line of provocations. They had dug up trenches all around Kakanj. We never dug out a single trench. Our troops were sent to various locations but it never crossed our mind to fight with our own neighbours in our own municipality. To this day, I have very good relations with Croats and Serbs I work with. I treat them and think of them as my colleagues, and I'm coming back now to the HVO. They created non-stop provocations, from digging trenches, shooting during the night, some people were murdered at some point, some deportations took place. I can't tell you everything that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, in those days in May, you were the chief of intelligence of the 3rd Battalion; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the battalion's intelligence department.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And you also told us this morning that you were also interested, as you should, about the enemy, you know, what their forces are. But let me ask you about your own forces. On that day, 18th -- mid-May 1993, watt the 3rd Battalion also reinforced by parts of the 2nd Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, on that day, on the day of the incident, I went to the 309th Mountain Brigade and I was there all the time. I didn't return to the motel, I was gathering intelligence from the field because all the information, all the intelligence arrived in the 309th. As to who went to the motel, who left the motel, I don't know, I wasn't there. On the following day when I arrived at the motel, I know that I didn't see any detainees there, I don't know whether they were exchanged but on the following day, there was no one there. I didn't see any members from other battalions at the motel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Let me follow-up first on what you just told us. At what time did you leave your headquarters at the motel in order to go to the headquarters of the 309th Brigade? What time in the day was that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was perhaps about 3.00 or 4.00 in the afternoon. I don't know exactly. I really don't know the precise time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And the next day, you returned to the motel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And at what time did you return to the motel?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was perhaps around noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So the information you have basically about the events at the motel in that evening, that night, that morning is basically what others told you?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I don't think I have understood you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Okay. Because you were not at the motel after 3.00, 4.00 in the afternoon before you returned the next day, all the information you relayed to us today about incidents of occurring, you know, to people at the motel is what other people told you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let me just go back to the question I asked you previously. Are you saying you don't know whether parts of the 2nd Battalion reinforced the 3rd Battalion or are you saying there was no reinforcement of the 2nd Battalion into the 3rd Battalion in any combat or other activities in those days?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, I'm not saying that that didn't occur on that day. I'm not saying that because I don't know. I wasn't there at the time. I don't know who went to the motel, who left the motel, so I don't know because I didn't see that. I can only tell you about what I saw or about what I heard but I can't say anything about the 2nd Battalion because I didn't see any members of the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: But you are the chief of intelligence of that battalion. How can you advise your commander about how to fight the enemy if you don't even know who is part of your own troops?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know if you have been following everything I have been saying from the outset. I told you that I worked as an operator in the Kakanj power plant but it just so happened that I became involved in intelligence matters. We weren't professionals, we didn't have a professional army, we were training and unfortunately, we had to go to war. So if you consider me to be an intelligence officer and yet you believe that I have certain shortcomings, the shortcomings are the result of the fact that I was an amateur. But it's not only that there were amateurs in the 7th Muslim Brigade, all the men in all the brigades were amateurs. 99 per cent of the officers were not professionals. There were very few professionals.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Let me ask about what you told us this morning on the beating of that HVO person. Now you told us you were informed by somebody that this had occurred. Can you tell us who informed you about the beating of this HVO soldier, what you have described as an "accident." Who told you that information?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Are you asking me about a member of the HVO who was beaten or a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade who was beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No, about a member of the HVO or a civilian, a Croat civilian.

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't saying anything about that. I said that I had information when I was in the command of the 309th Brigade, this is what I heard from one of the soldiers who appeared there and he said that the military police had brought in members of the HVO to the motel. He didn't mention any civilians. I didn't see whether this person was a civilian or a soldier. All I know that I was told that they were HVO members because, according to what I heard, they also found certain weapons on these men when they brought them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And my question again is who told you that? You said "one of the soldiers who appeared there." Was that one of the members of the military police?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: No, he wasn't a member of the military police. I can't remember now but he was one of our men. Some of our troops from the motel would go up to the 309th to see what was happening there because they were worried about their families. They were afraid that a conflict would break out and as they would go up there, I heard that the police had brought someone in in order to exchange them for their own men.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Didn't you tell us this morning that an accident occurred? Do you remember that? Because some people were provoked because of the -- an MP was injured and you explained the way that provocation resulted in an accident; do you remember having told us that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, who was the victim of that accident?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the victims were certainly more the members of the HVO rather than members of the other side. I couldn't see the state that they were in. There were a number of men, I don't know how many exactly -- well, let's say there was one man who had been beaten up and the others had been captured. But this young man or rather this policeman from the 7th Muslim Brigade, I saw him myself and he was unable to walk. They had beaten him on the elbows and the knees. The French Battalion took him out from the personnel carrier on a stretcher.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm still not entirely sure. The way I understand your testimony is there were several beatings and people were beaten who were part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that the witness has already said on a number of occasions that he didn't see those individuals. He didn't mention any beating. My learned colleague is now putting a question to the witness and making certain suggestions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. President, I'm just confused because I understood the witness before the break, in chief, saying that an incident happened to a member of the military police of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade, that he was beaten up, and that this had provoked some other members of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade to beat up an HVO member and he described that as an accident. That's what I heard the witness saying this morning and I would just like him to confirm and clarify what perhaps is a confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Can you follow me, Mr. Kulovic?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So initially there was an incident which involved an HVO military police member who was a victim of a beating, I think he had bruises on the elbows and other injuries; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't an HVO member, he was a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade, a member of the 7th Muslim Brigade was beaten up by the HVO. That is what I witnessed when he was taken to the command of the 309th Brigade. The French Battalion of UNPROFOR brought in a member of the police force. He'd been kidnapped by the HVO. They'd beaten him up and he was then taken to the command of the 309th Brigade. That's what I saw but I didn't see anything at Motel Sretno, I saw what happened up in the command of the 309th Brigade. I saw that with my very own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, I understood that far. And then you told us that this incident provoked the beating of an HVO victim and you described that beating as an accident?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is all very confusing. Just a minute. I will ask the witness some questions because it is a little confusing. With regard to your answers to the questions put to you, as far as I have understood your testimony, initially there were members of the military police who had been encircled by the HVO and you said that they went to the Sretno Motel, there were through or four of them, and said that they were there because friends of theirs had been encircled by the HVO. And you said that you then went to the 309th Brigade to see what the problem was. Is that, in fact, how all of this started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Should I answer the question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, do answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, it happened just as you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. That's what I understood. And then when you were in the 309th Brigade, according to what you said, a member of the 7th Brigade arrived, a member who had been beaten up by the HVO and you added that this member of the 7th Brigade was carried on a stretcher. Can you confirm that as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I can confirm that in the evening, UNPROFOR brought a member of the police force from 7th Muslim Brigade to the command of the 309th Brigade. They drove him there in their personnel carrier. I was present and I saw them taking this man out of the personnel carrier on a stretcher because he was unable to walk. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Later, they transferred him to a hospital in Kakanj or Zenica, I don't know where. But he was transferred to a hospital. That is what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So that is the situation. I will now give the floor to the Prosecution again. Things are clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Were you aware, Mr. Kulovic, that a member of the 7th Muslim Mountain Brigade was also beating somebody else, was beating a member of the HVO or a Croat civilian. Have you heard about that during that stay?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I haven't understood the question. Where? What area?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: This morning, you told us that an accident occurred, an unfortunate accident; do you remember having testified that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. My testimony about what happened at the motel concerns all of the events and all of these events were unfortunate, the blockade of -- or the encirclement of members of the 7th and the events around the motel, so all of these events, unfortunate events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So are you saying you don't remember that there was an unfortunate incident in which a member of the HVO or a Croat civilian has been beaten. Are you saying that didn't happen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness has just clarified the situation in response to your very precise questions. My learned colleague is trying to confuse the witness again. He did not mention any civilians or HVO members being beaten up. We are wasting time discussing these matters. I think we have to try and expedite the proceedings and deal with this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The question the Prosecution put to you concerns two incidents, we have two incidents. The first incident was when you were at Motel Sretno, the military police arrived and they said that they had been encircled, shots had been fired; that was the first incident. The second incident was when you were at the 309th Brigade and the French Battalion, the UNPROFOR French Battalion delivered a member of the military police from the 7th Brigade who had been beaten up by the HVO. That is the second incident. And now, the Prosecution is putting a question to you that concerns another incident. The Prosecution is asking you whether, as far as you know, you heard that HVO members had been beaten up in the Sretno Motel. This is another incident. So that is the question. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not a problem. I immediately said that I didn't see that but I heard and I know that there was such an incident. HVO members were brought in and beaten up. I don't deny the fact. That is the truth. But I myself did not see this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There we are.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: I'm really obliged to you for bringing that out of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And who told you about that incident?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Again, I don't understand your question. Do you mean when I was in the 309th Brigade, up there or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. Kulovic, you just responded to the -- to Mr. President's questions and I quote you, "HVO members were brought in and beaten up." And you said beforehand, "I didn't see that but I heard." My question is: From whom did you hear that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: On the following day, the day after the incident, I arrived at the Sretno Motel in the afternoon and members of our battalion told me about this unfortunate incident down there. They told me about the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And do you remember whom from your battalion told you that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, it's very difficult for me to answer the question, not because I don't want to but I can't remember. I really can't remember. You know, I don't want to give you the wrong answer. I can't remember who it was but I know that when I arrived there, I was told by someone that such an incident had occurred.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And why were you told? Why did these soldiers come to you? Was it in your capacity as --

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: No, perhaps you haven't understood me. They did not report to me. It's not as if I arrived at the motel and then someone reported this to me, because I wasn't responsible for such matters. That's the first thing. And then secondly, well this was something that I just heard as I was passing through. It wasn't an official report of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And when you say you weren't responsible for that matter, who was responsible for that matter?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, according to the chain of command, well, you know exactly what the hierarchy is, and as to who was responsible, I couldn't really say now. I don't know. I couldn't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Who is responsible for detaining prisoners, who is in charge of detaining prisoners in your unit, in your battalion?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Look, no one ordered those policemen, no one ordered the military policemen to capture certain HVO members. This is something they did on their own initiative. I don't know how else I could explain it but it was done on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You just said that you think they did it on their own initiative, why do you say that? Why do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, look, I'll go back to what I was saying before. On the following day I arrived in the battalion and when I spoke to the troops and certain colleagues, unofficially I found out that military policemen had done what they had done on their own initiative, without having received an order to act in such a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And from whom did you find out unofficially that they had done that on their own initiative?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He's already answered the question by saying that he didn't know. That's what the Defence would like to say. Don't insist, as the witness has said, that he cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, do you know whether there was an investigation done into the beating of these HVO people? Have you heard about any investigation?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, I assume that an investigation was launched, but this is an assumption. I'm not sure, and no one informed me of the fact, but I assume that an investigation should have been launched but I personally know nothing about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Who was the chief of security within your battalion?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Huso Lihovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: So your function was only related to intelligence, you were only the chief of intelligence and there was a second chief and he was the chief of security?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: At that time in the army, the intelligence officer was separate from the security officer; these were two separate posts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, let me go back to the answer you gave just half a minute ago. You said that "I assume that an investigation should have been launched but I personally know nothing about this." Now, are you saying it should have been launched or in your opinion, it must be launched? You just said "I assume" so if you can clarify what your position is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has already answered the question. He said that he assumes that there should have been an investigation but he says that he knows nothing about this so there is no point for the Prosecution to demand whether it should have been launched or must have been launched.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: There are two differences, whether an investigation has been launched and I think he said he assumes, and the other one is whether it should have been done because I assume it's a serious thing, the beating. So my question is he, as the chief of intelligence, whether he thinks today in this court, that this incident should have been investigated. That's my question to this witness about this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kulovic, when you returned to the Sretno Motel, you heard that there had been an incident and in response to a question from the Prosecution, you said that you assumed that perhaps there was an investigation or perhaps an investigation should have been launched. So were you aware of the fact that an investigation was launched or were you not aware of any investigation because you aren't responsible for such matters? What could you say about the investigation that was, perhaps, launched or perhaps not? What sort of information could you provide us with about this? Firstly, did this fall within your competence and if not, what did you know about a non -- investigation that was launched that should have been launched [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally -- I wasn't responsible for the events around the motel. As an intelligence officer, I did not deal with security matters. As far as the investigation is concerned, all I can do is repeat that is that I wasn't provided with any information but I assume that at the time there were intensive preparations for combat. It was a long time ago so I couldn't answer that question. I can only say that I don't know whether an investigation was launched or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have about five more minutes with this witness. I don't know whether we should stop for the recess or whether I should continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Continue for another five minutes and then we'll take a break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, were you questioned by anybody by your chief of security, by any authorities about this incident, about what you know or don't know about this incident?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody ever asked anything of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, since you had heard about a serious thing happening in your -- in that headquarters, did you personally report what you had heard about that to somebody?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know from my level who I was supposed to report things to. I don't even understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: If you are an officer in the ABiH army, were you not, at the time, one of the section chiefs, if I may call it, so in a battalion, and you are hearing about the mistreatment of prisoners in your headquarters, don't you think it's your obligation to report it to your commander?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I believe my commander was aware of it. There was no need for me to inform him. I mean battalion commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: You must have been very sure about that, that he knew about that incident.

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you again, I did not speak personally to the commander about this but he was somewhere around the motel himself. I supposed that he knew about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Now, you talked about - and that's my last question or small issue - that there were HVO soldiers held or detained at the motel. Were there civilians among these HVO officers? I know you weren't there, but were you informed that there were also civilians among the people who were held at the motel?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Nobody told me, they only mentioned the HVO. HVO can be used as a broad term. A soldier of the HVO may wear civilian clothing when at home, for instance. When I come back home, I, too, shed my uniform and put on civilian clothes. So I don't know whether in this instance whether they were real civilians or whether they were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: And my last question is, when did the military police who came from Zenica to Kakanj, when they left the motel, when did they leave the hotel after all this commotion occurred?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: We are coming back to that again and I'm telling you, again, I didn't go back to the motel that night, I went home to sleep and when I returned the next day, there were no military police within the perimeter of the motel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your answers. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are going to take the break and we are going to resume around 1300 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Waespi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, with your leave, I just have one question about the location to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Just one last question, Mr. Kulovic. You told us a lot about the 309th Brigade, the headquarters where you spent sometime on that day in May. Can you tell us where exactly the headquarters of the 309th Brigade was and how far away from the Motel Sretno that was?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: As for the distance from the motel, it was maybe 2 kilometres, say; I don't know exactly. But the place where the command was, was what we called the cultural hall. Or let me be more precise, the town library of Kakanj was around there and that was the precise location of the command of the 309th Brigade at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions for redirect. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Then I have some questions for the sake of clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You explained that the military policemen had arrived, there were three or four of them, and they said that they had been attacked and encircled by the HVO and for a number of hours, they remained there. Do you know what became of those who had been encircled? Did you receive any subsequent information about the encircled men?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: The information that I have from -- or rather about the policemen who remained encircled is that the HVO had come from Catici, from that direction, and made a full circle around them. They hid into a catering establishment. The HVO managed to drag out one of them from this catering establishment and take him in the direction of Sutjeska. Nobody told me anything about any abuse of these men because the UNPROFOR did not have any such information. The UNPROFOR didn't have any information that the members of the 7th Brigade were abused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before that time in 1993, were there any important clashes between the ABiH and the HVO in the area of Kakanj or was that the first serious indent because you said you the men were afraid of what might happen to the general population in case of a serious clash. Was that the only incident or were there others?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that I mentioned in one of my statements, prior statements, something about it. Before the aggression, we lived together, Serbs, Bosniaks, Croats, and we kept guard around our villages. From the time the HVO was established, somebody ordered these neighbours of ours not to keep guard together with us any longer but to retreat instead to the highest elevations around Kakanj where the population was mostly Croat. So from that moment until that last incident, there were quite a lot of incidents in Kakanj. Maybe I mentioned this before, maybe not: At the time of shooting, tracing -- tracer bullets and other ammunition was used and the HVO pulled out heavier weapons taking them through Muslim villages. For instance, on one occasion, Croats who know that Muslims do not eat pork killed a pig and took it through Kakanj. They created different incidents as well. For instance, on the occasion of the given of the solemn oath, they blocked Kakanj and they placed snipers on every high-rise building in Kakanj. This I know with 100 per cent certainty. So there were all sorts of provocations and as our people used to say, there were 100 of alarms and thank God nothing more serious, even more serious happened. But even what happened is quite enough.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said in response to Defence questions that military policemen had arrived to arrest deserters from the 7th Brigade who had failed to report back to duty so that was the reason why the military police came in the first place. Was it not?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: According to my information, they came in order to take into custody a number of army members from the village of Papratnica and maybe some other villages, that's the information I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are telling us that the next day when you returned to Sretno Motel, you learned there had been an incident between the military police and members of the HVO where blows were exchanged. Later on, was this incident the subject of talk and comments or was nothing more said about it? What can you tell us about the aftermath of this incident?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: In the days that followed after the incident, fighting intensified outside of Kakanj so that units were preparing for movement. I know, for instance, that one unit was going to the battlefield in Ovnak and the preparations were very hurried and intense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So when you returned, that's what you said, but I want to be sure and to hear your confirmation. When you returned, there were neither military policemen nor HVO members at the Sretno Motel, there were only soldiers from your own battalion. That's the scene you found the next day.

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And with Mr. Catic, brigade commander, you never discussed the problem again?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Catic was the commander of this battalion and we never discussed this event, the two much us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You also said that there were two different structures, intelligence - that was your responsibility - and the military side security where your other colleagues were in charge. So when you learned -- in fact, if you had been present on the spot and found out that your men had been taken away, what would you have done?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: If I had been there, it is quite certain that I wouldn't bring in those members to the motel and even if I had done so, I would have made sure that no incident occurred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And you never discussed this with the security men? Was that, in fact, the problem, that you didn't discuss it with the security?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Even on the day when those policemen arrived, I don't believe I saw him near the motel. That day when the military police came from Zenica, I don't remember seeing him. As for the next day, I'm not certain. But I know for sure I had no contact with him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But since you, yourself, went to the headquarters of the 309th Brigade, which is just 200 metres from the motel, was there an officer in charge when you were leaving? Can you remember that? Was there an officer present there when you were leaving to see what was going on at the 309th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I was at the headquarters of the command of the 309th all the time, Commander Catic and Deputy Commander Kasim Alajbegovic came and went. I think the security officer also came and went but I'm not sure about him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No questions, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Defence team of General Hadzihasanovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a couple of questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kulovic, in response to the questions asked by the Trial Chamber, you said that this event had been preceded by a number of provocations. Did I understand you correctly as saying that all those provocations that you described were created by the HVO after they were established in Kakanj?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that the 309th Brigade and the municipal staff of Kakanj as well as your own battalion made every effort to resolve these provocations and avoid conflict? Is my understanding of your testimony correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also in response to the questions asked by the Presiding Judge, you stated the reasons why you acted that way. You said namely that you had your hands full with the one enemy you were handling. Did you mean to imply your fighting with the Serb army?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Army units from Kakanj were, in fact, holding the front line against the Serb army over a considerable territory towards Vozeca [phoen] and Breza?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on the Vogosca battlefield we held the front line over 30 kilometres long and we had a considerable length of the front line from Visoko towards Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And while you were defending this important front line, as you said, the HVO was getting entrenched within this territory at the highest elevations from which they could control both Kakanj and the surrounding villages?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Correct. If I may clarify, the HVO created a genuine military defence line with entrenchments, with positions of heavy weaponry. An anti-aircraft machine-gun was positioned at an elevation in such a way as to have within range the entire town, so that is absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Since you were an intelligence officer, your principal task, and the principal task of the men under you in the intelligence organ, was to gather information about the enemy, both the Serb army and the HVO. Is that the reason why you are absolutely certain about this information concerning the conduct of the HVO?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: You could define it that way.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In view of this information and your efforts to avoid this conflict, were you also acting that way because parts of Kakanj municipality were the only place through which humanitarian convoys could pass towards Vares and on to Eastern Bosnia, and if that road was cut off or blocked, a large number of troops would have been deprived of any assistance at all?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you another thing: As an intelligence officer in the previous period, especially after the offensive carried out by the HVO in the Lasva Valley, did you learn about the intentions of the HVO to link up forces from Kiseljak and Busovaca with the forces in Vares?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I suppose the Prosecution will say that the Judges did not ask anything about this and that you are going beyond the scope of their questions. If you are asking these questions, it is for the sake of background information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President, since you mentioned incidents, and the efforts of the army to prevent them, I am invoking incidents that speak to the planned behaviour of the HVO and that is the context in which the witness has been answering. But I'm not going to insist. I have only one more question related to the arrival of the military police at Kakanj on the 18th of May.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I want one thing to be clear to me: You heard on that day that 10 or so military policemen had arrived on that day with a very specific task, that is, to bring in soldiers who had failed to report for duty at time?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear about their arrival, I saw a couple of them and I found out that there were 10 or 12 in total.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify this. Those military policemen were in the 7th Muslim Brigade in Zenica; correct?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You, just like other battalions from the 7th Muslim and other brigades had your own military police platoons?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: They were not real platoons, they were there in order to provide some sort of security. We needed them for our purposes to secure buildings, to bring in people into custody, in minor incidents, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So all that you have been describing involves the military policemen from Zenica, there were no military policemen of your own involved?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: Everything involves the brigade military police from Zenica but since I was not at the motel while it was all happening, I cannot claim here that not a single of our soldiers had approached and gotten involved in some way, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence of General Kubura.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No further questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, Mr. President, I have just one more question and it has to do with duties performed by the battalion.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Presiding Judge asked you about the security sector. Since you said that you had no experts or not enough experts, is it true that in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your battalion, there was no lawyer, no legal person?

utterances.speaker: FUAD KULOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't have any.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Any of the other counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No questions, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kulovic, I will now thank you on behalf of the Chamber for having come to testify for General Kubura. You have our best wishes for a safe journey back home. I will now ask the usher to see you out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we have a couple of minutes left to discuss the planning for the rest of the week. I believe we have about a dozen witnesses of which three at least under Rule 92 bis and around seven viva voce witnesses. Is my reckoning correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are correct, Mr. President. But before that, we have these documents that have been shown to the witness and we wish to tender them as Defence Exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there are two documents indeed. So Prosecution, there are two documents, one is dated 5th September, 1992, and the other is another date in September, 1992. Any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. WAESPI
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please give us the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first is dated 5 September 1992, it will be DK [Previous interpretation continues] [In English] 57/E. As to the second document, it's dated the 5th of September, 1992 is entitled "Order on appointment" and receives the reference number DK58 with an English translation DK58/E. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I give the floor to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have no further witnesses for this session until the end of the week, that is by the end of the week, we will give you our work plan for the next week and the list of witnesses. We have discussed witness statements under 92 bis with our colleagues and we had agreed to hold a meeting on Monday morning and we will keep the Trial Chamber informed accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Are we at least sure that on Monday afternoon, we will have a witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will confirm that no later than the day after tomorrow but probably tomorrow, the entire plan for the whole week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Yes, registrar, please could you look again at the numbers that you gave the document the 5th September, is it really DK57? And the other document ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I repeat, the numbers were given ... [In English] The first document is admitted into evidence, it's dated the 1st of December, 1992 is admitted under DK57 with an English translation, DK 57/E. The second document is dated the 5th of September, 1992, is entitled order on appointment and is admitted into evidence under the reference DK58 with an English translation DK58/E. I hope that's -- this clarifies. [Interpretation] I hope that clarifies everything, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We are also waiting to receive Defence counsel's written submissions on the Prosecution motion to reopen its case in order to tender documents into evidence. If I have understood the Defence correctly, they need 15 days to provide these written submissions. Could Mr. Bourgon when Defence counsel will be filing these submissions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, in accordance with the meeting, 65 ter meeting held last week, I think that we will require 14 days before we can file these submissions. I think that we will be able to file these written submissions by the 6th of May at the latest. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well then, Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The 6th of May is Friday and that would be 14 days. So for Mr. Kubura, we will certainly file the response by Friday as well. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are there any other issues that either the parties would like to raise. Mr. Bourgon. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Last week, General Hadzihasanovic's Defence filed a certain number of translations received from CLSS. There were 70 documents, Mr. President, and we would like definite exhibit numbers for 22 of them, whereas as far as the others are concerned, they concern our request to have documents admitted into evidence. We asked for the registry to provide us with confirmation with regard to the 37 outstanding documents. They should be ready by the -- by Friday of this week at the latest. As soon as we receive these 37 documents, we will serve copies on the Prosecution immediately. And we will then file our final written submissions. As the Chamber demanded at the hearing on the 22nd of April. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis are there any other issues you would like to address.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Not at this time, Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And Mr. Kubura's Defence counsel, any issues to raise? Very well. I invite you to return for the hearing that should start next Monday at 2.15 p.m. And we hope that we will have a witness for Monday. Thank you.
